conventions.convention: The canonical form is ω_N = Σ dq_i^a ∧ dp_i^a, with Hamiltonian convention ι_XH ω_N = dH_N. The pair potential W is smooth, even and periodic; K = −∇W is odd and vanishes at zero. The interaction coefficient is 1/N.
Physical coordinates have SI units. Dimensionless coordinates are x = q/L, v = p/P₀ and s = t/τ₀, where τ₀ = mL/P₀; Φ(x) = mW(Lx)/P₀² and k = −∇Φ.

Z = T^d × R^d carries its product Borel sigma algebra and distance d_Z((x,v),(y,w)) = d_T(x,y) + |v−w|. P₁(Z) requires a finite first velocity moment. W₁ is the infimum of coupling costs; existence of a minimizing coupling is not assumed.

Finite-N densities and marginals are normalized probabilities relative to canonical phase volume. All phase derivatives of the initial density have rapid momentum decay, uniformly in position. The density-measure and completed-product arguments retain countable choice.

The BBGKY marginals integrate out labeled particles without combinatorial normalization factors. Their external interaction coefficient is (N−k)/N; at k = N the external term is absent and f_(N+1) is not used.

The preparation uses one countably infinite sequence of mutually independent coordinates with common compactly supported law μ₀, taking its first N coordinates for each N. The construction explicitly assumes full Choice. These are adopted model assumptions, not observations.

Propagation of chaos concerns each fixed k and bounded-Lipschitz tests with the sum metric on Z^k, uniformly only on finite time intervals. The smooth-density hierarchy branch and compact iid limit branch are separate conditional conclusions.

load_bearing.statement: Fix d ≥ 1, L > 0, m > 0 and a smooth even periodic pair potential W. The Hamiltonian is Σ_i |p_i|²/(2m) + N⁻¹Σ_(i<j) W(q_i−q_j); dimensionless equations are x_i′ = v_i and v_i′ = N⁻¹Σ_(j≠i) k(x_i−x_j).

Under the stated countable-choice and smooth periodic model assumptions, the Hamiltonian ODE has a unique complete smooth flow for all real times, preserves Liouville volume and commutes with particle permutations. Symmetric normalized smooth densities with all-phase-derivative rapid momentum tails retain these properties under transport on finite time slabs.

Every Borel probability μ₀ on Z with finite first velocity moment has a unique global characteristic evolution for the specified smooth periodic force; its push-forward law is narrowly continuous, retains a finite first velocity moment and satisfies the stated weak Vlasov identity. Smooth initial densities with all velocity moments give the stated classical smooth branch.

For μ₀,ν₀ ∈ P₁(Z), W₁(μ_s,ν_s) ≤ exp((1+2A)|s|)W₁(μ₀,ν₀). Finite-N empirical evolution satisfies the same comparison with the characteristic law. Narrowly continuous weak solutions with locally bounded first velocity moments are characteristic evolutions and are unique.

For compactly supported iid preparation, expected initial W₁ error is at most δ + (D_K/2)√(M_δ/N), with M_δ ≤ C_K δ^(−2d). The empirical error converges almost surely uniformly on finite time intervals, and each fixed-k marginal satisfies the stated collision-plus-Wasserstein bounded-Lipschitz estimate.

The normalized marginals of the stated symmetric smooth rapidly decreasing finite-N density satisfy the exact hierarchy with internal coefficient 1/N and external coefficient (N−k)/N, without factorization; the external term is absent for k = N.

A time-continuous force on J × T^d with jointly continuous state derivatives of every order, bounded with those derivatives on the compact time interval, gives a unique second-order flow on that interval, smooth in initial state with uniformly bounded derivatives and a backward inverse.
Two Borel probabilities on Z agreeing on every smooth position-periodic test with compact velocity support agree on all Borel sets.

concerns.concern: The Statement takes E sup_{|s|≤T} W₁(μ_N(s),μ_s), but the proof does not explicitly establish measurability of this random supremum. This is a routine omitted justification: establish continuity of the empirical coupling cost in its finitely many atoms, continuity in time on the compact-support finite-time slab, and then replace the time supremum by a countable dense-time supremum. The partition bound alone does not establish measurability of the cost defined as an infimum over couplings.
